info.text:
Myth: bonds are safe, so they can't lose value.

In 2022 the Bloomberg US Aggregate bond index returned -13.01%, its worst year since it began in 1976 (the old record was -2.92% in 1994).
Long-term Treasuries fell harder: the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) returned -31.4% in 2022.
Why: when rates rise, existing bond prices fall. FINRA's rule of thumb: price moves about 1% per year of duration for each 1-point rate change. Our math: a duration-6 fund, rates up 2 points, $10,000 becomes about $8,800.
A high-quality bond held to maturity repays face value barring default; most bond funds have no maturity date.

Sources: State Street SPDR index data, Bloomberg, iShares (TLT), FINRA.
News and education, not financial advice.
